tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Significant management estimates and judgments are involved to determine the provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, and valuation allowances.

An assessment is performed on a quarterly basis to determine the likelihood of realizing deferred tax assets. We assess the probability of realizing deferred tax assets by evaluating historical income after adjusting for certain nonrecurring items for purposes of projecting future income, our intent and ability to implement tax planning strategies, and performing scheduling of the reversal of temporary differences. We also evaluate negative evidence, such as the expiration of historical operating loss or tax credit carryforwards, that could indicate an inability to realize deferred tax assets. Based on the combined assessment, we recognize valuation allowances for deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not such benefit will not be realized in future periods.

Actual income taxes could vary from estimated amounts due to the future impacts of various items, including changes in income tax laws, forecasted financial conditions, and results of operations in future periods, as well as results of audits and examinations of filed tax returns by taxing authorities. See Note 4 to the Annual Financial Statements for additional information on income taxes.

tax.text: Adjusted EBITDA is computed as net income (loss) adjusted, among other things, for certain: (i) nonrecurring charges; (ii) non-recurring gains; (iii) non-cash and other items; (iv) unusual market events; (v) any depreciation, amortization, or accretion; (vi) mark-to-market gains or losses; (vii) gains and losses on the NDT; (viii) gains and losses on asset sales, dispositions, and asset retirement; (ix) impairments, obsolescence, and net realizable value charges; (x) interest expense; (xi) income taxes; (xii) legal settlements, liquidated damages, and contractual terminations; (xiii) development expenses; (xiv) noncontrolling interests, except where otherwise noted; and (xv) other adjustments. intro.text: Talen is a leading independent power producer and energy infrastructure company dedicated to powering the future. We own and operate approximately 13.1 GW of power infrastructure in the United States, including 2.2 GW of nuclear power and a significant dispatchable fossil fleet. We produce and sell electricity, capacity, and ancillary services into wholesale U.S. power markets, with our generation fleet principally located in the Mid-Atlantic, Ohio, and Montana. Our team is committed to generating power safely and reliably and delivering the most value per megawatt produced. Talen is also powering the digital infrastructure revolution. We are well-positioned to serve this growing industry, as artificial intelligence data centers increasingly demand more reliable power.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Significant management estimates and judgments are involved to determine the provision for income taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities, and valuation allowances.

An assessment is performed on a quarterly basis to determine the likelihood of realizing deferred tax assets. We assess the probability of realizing deferred tax assets by evaluating historical income after adjusting for certain nonrecurring items for purposes of projecting future income, our intent and ability to implement tax planning strategies, and performing scheduling of the reversal of temporary differences. We also evaluate negative evidence, such as the expiration of historical operating loss or tax credit carryforwards, that could indicate an inability to realize deferred tax assets. Based on the combined assessment, we recognize valuation allowances for deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not such benefit will not be realized in future periods.

Actual income taxes could vary from estimated amounts due to the future impacts of various items, including changes in income tax laws, forecasted financial conditions, and results of operations in future periods, as well as results of audits and examinations of filed tax returns by taxing authorities. See Note 7 to the Annual Financial Statements for additional information on income taxes.

wc.text: On January 15, 2026, we entered into the Cornerstone Merger Agreement to acquire from affiliates of Energy Capital Partners (“ECP”) the 875 MW Waterford Energy Center and 456 MW Darby Generating Station, both located in Ohio, and the 1,120 MW Lawrenceburg Power Plant located in Indiana, for an aggregate purchase price of $3.45 billion, consisting of $2.55 billion in cash, subject to working capital and other customary adjustments, and 2,400,000 shares of Talen common stock, valued at approximately $900 million at the time of the entry into the Cornerstone Merger Agreement. lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
